body: Newer houses have drywall: it comes off in sheets and loads quickly. Older St. Louis houses often have plaster on wood lath, which is heavier, dustier and slower, and fills the truck faster. Tell us which you have, or send a photo of a spot where the wall is open.

We take it to the studs and leave the framing, wiring and plumbing for your electrician and plumber. Need the framing out too, to open up a room? That's [wall removal](/services/demolition/wall-removal/).

sections.h2: How much does drywall removal cost?
body: The tear-out itself is quoted per job. Debris hauling starts at {quarter} for a quarter load. {fit:three-quarter:drywall} {examplesNote}

sections.h2: Testing older walls first
body: Plaster walls are common in older homes, and so are the things to test for before they come down. Paint from before 1978 can contain lead, and a test before demolition tells you what you're dealing with. Some older joint compound and wall texture contains asbestos. Have an inspector test it first: we don't test for asbestos, remove it or haul it.
Shut off and cap the electric and water to any wall we're opening. Ceilings coming down too? See [ceiling removal](/services/demolition/ceiling-removal/).

body: Ceramic and porcelain tile, including tile set in a mortar bed. Nailed or glued hardwood, floating laminate and engineered floors, sheet vinyl and vinyl plank, carpet and pad. Tell us what's under it, like the subfloor or concrete, and whether the subfloor stays.
Carpet only? That's a simpler pull-up: [carpet removal](/services/junk-removal/carpet-removal/).

sections.h2: How much does flooring removal cost?
body: Pulling up the floor is labor, quoted per job from photos, because a glued-down hardwood floor and a floating laminate aren't the same work. Hauling it is priced by the load, from {quarter}. {heavy}

sections.h2: Old tile and adhesive: test first
body: Older homes often have 9-inch vinyl floor tiles, sheet flooring or black adhesive under a newer floor. Those materials can contain asbestos. That calls for an asbestos inspection before work starts. Testing and abatement aren't part of what we do, and we can't haul asbestos. If you're not sure what's down there, get it tested before any flooring is pulled.
Redoing the whole kitchen or bathroom? See [kitchen demolition](/services/demolition/kitchen-demolition/) and [bathroom demolition](/services/demolition/bathroom-demolition/).

intro: We take out non-load-bearing walls, drywall or plaster, studs and plates, to open up a kitchen, a living room or a basement, and haul the debris away, across St. Louis City, St. Louis County and St. Charles County. Send photos and we quote the labor; the haul is priced by the load.

sections.h2: Opening up a room
body: A partition wall between the kitchen and dining room, a closet you don't need, a half wall on the stairs or framing in an unfinished basement. We take the wall covering off, then the studs and plates, and leave the floor and ceiling edges ready for your contractor to patch.
If wiring, plumbing or ductwork runs through the wall, it has to be rerouted or capped before we start. That's for your electrician, plumber or HVAC tech.

sections.h2: Is the wall load-bearing?
body: We take out walls that don't hold up the house. If a wall carries the floor or roof above it, the support has to be planned by an engineer or a contractor before it comes out. If you're not sure, have it checked first, and tell us what they found.
Clues worth asking about: a wall that runs across the floor joists above it, sits in the middle of the house, or has another wall stacked on top of it upstairs.

sections.h2: How much does wall removal cost?
body: The wall removal is labor, quoted per job from photos. The debris is hauled by the load, starting at {quarter} for a quarter of the truck.
Homes built before 1978 can have lead paint, and older joint compound can contain asbestos. Have both tested before demo day: we don't test for, remove or haul asbestos.
Taking more than one wall out? See [interior demolition](/services/demolition/interior-demolition/) or a [whole-house gut](/services/demolition/whole-house-gut/).

intro: We take down ceilings: drywall, plaster and lath, drop-ceiling grids and tiles, and ceilings ruined by a roof or plumbing leak, and haul the debris away, anywhere in the St. Louis area. Ceiling demo is messy, so we plan the dust and the debris before we start.

sections.h2: Drywall, plaster and drop ceilings
body: Drywall ceilings come down in sheets. Plaster and lath ceilings are heavy and come down in chunks, often with years of dust and old insulation above them. Drop ceilings come out grid and all. Tell us what's above the ceiling: an attic, a floor or ductwork.
We take it to the joists and leave the wiring and light boxes for your electrician to make safe.

sections.h2: Popcorn ceilings: test before scraping
body: Textured or popcorn ceilings in older homes can contain asbestos. Don't scrape or sand one until it's been tested. An inspector should test it before we start. We can't test for, remove or haul asbestos.
If the house was built before 1978, get the paint tested for lead first. Plaster ceilings in older homes are often painted many times over.

sections.h2: How much does ceiling removal cost?
body: Taking the ceiling down is labor, quoted per job from photos. The debris is hauled by the load, from {quarter} for a quarter of the truck to {full} for the whole {maxYards}-yard truck.

Walls coming down too? See [drywall and plaster removal](/services/demolition/drywall-removal/). A ceiling ruined by a leak usually means the walls got wet too: [fire and water damage tear-out](/services/demolition/fire-water-damage-tear-out/).

intro: We tear out finished basements, drywall, paneling, framing, carpet, drop ceilings and built-ins, back to the foundation walls and slab, and haul it all away, across St. Louis City, St. Louis County and St. Charles County. It's for remodels and for basements that took on water.

sections.h2: Finished basements, back to the block
body: Drywall or paneling, the stud walls, carpet and pad, laminate or tile, the drop ceiling, a wet bar, a basement bathroom and built-in shelving. Tell us what stays, like the furnace room, the laundry area or a wall you like, and we work around it.
Everything comes up the stairs or out the walkout door. {access}

sections.h2: After a flood or a sump pump failure
body: Wet drywall, insulation and carpet should come out quickly. If there's an insurance claim, check with your adjuster before anything is removed. If there's visible mold, have it assessed before tear-out; we're a demolition crew, not a mold remediation company.
Just the soaked boxes and furniture? That's a [basement cleanout](/services/cleanouts/basement-cleanout/), priced by the load.

sections.h2: How much does a basement tear-out cost?
body: The tear-out itself is quoted per job. Hauling the debris is priced by how much of the truck it fills, from {quarter}.

Older basements can have floor tile, pipe insulation or other materials that contain asbestos. We don't do asbestos testing or abatement, and we can't haul asbestos. Testing is handled by an inspector before demolition. Painted paneling and trim from before 1978 should be tested for lead, too.

name: Fire and Water Damage Tear-Out

h1: Fire and water damage tear-out in St. Louis, MO
metaTitle: Fire & Water Damage Tear-Out, St. Louis MO
metaDescription: Fire and water damage tear-out in St. Louis: ruined drywall, flooring, cabinets and contents removed and hauled away so the rebuild can start.
intro: After a fire, a burst pipe or a roof leak, we tear out what's ruined, drywall, insulation, flooring, cabinets and damaged belongings, and haul it all away, anywhere in the St. Louis area. It clears the way for the drying crew and the rebuild.

sections.h2: What comes out
body: Wet or charred drywall and insulation, ceilings, flooring and pad, cabinets and vanities, trim and doors. Damaged furniture and belongings go on the same truck. Tell us what the restoration company or your contractor has marked to keep.
We're a demolition and hauling crew. Water extraction, drying, smoke cleaning and mold remediation are for a restoration company, and we can work alongside one.

sections.h2: Insurance and timing
body: Before anything is torn out, check with your insurance adjuster. Most want photos and an inspection of the damage first. Once they've seen it, we can quote from your photos and get it out quickly.
Shut off and cap the utilities to the damaged area. A fire-damaged structure may need to be cleared by your city's building department before anyone works inside it.

sections.h2: How much does damage tear-out cost?
body: Tearing it out is labor, and we quote that from photos. The haul is by the load, from {quarter} for a quarter of the truck to {full} for the full {maxYards}-yard truck, and a bigger job is more loads.

Older homes damaged by fire or water still need testing before tear-out. Have an inspector test it first: we don't test for asbestos, remove it or haul it. Lead paint was sold for homes until 1978, so test old painted surfaces before they're torn out.

h1: Whole-house interior gut in St. Louis, MO

intro: We gut whole houses: every room taken back to the studs, joists and subfloor, with the kitchen, bathrooms, flooring, ceilings and trim hauled away, across St. Louis City, St. Louis County and St. Charles County. sections.h2: To the studs, room by room
body: Drywall and plaster, ceilings, flooring, the kitchen, the bathrooms, interior doors, trim and built-ins. Tell us what the renovation keeps, like the stairs, original woodwork, windows or a wall, and we protect it.
Only one or two rooms? See [interior demolition](/services/demolition/interior-demolition/). The whole structure coming down? That's [house demolition](/services/demolition/house-demolition/).

sections.h2: Before a gut starts
body: Every utility in the area has to be shut off and capped. Permits vary from city to city. Tell us where the job is and we'll walk you through it.

A gut disturbs every wall, ceiling and floor at once, so test first. That calls for an asbestos inspection before work starts. Testing and abatement aren't part of what we do, and we can't haul asbestos. Homes built before 1978 can have lead paint, so have painted surfaces tested before demo day and tell us what the results say.

sections.h2: How much does a whole-house gut cost?
body: The tear-out is labor, quoted per job from photos; there's no price per square foot. The debris is hauled by the load at {full} for a full {maxYards}-yard truck, and a whole house takes several loads. {heavy}
We're {insured}, and we're glad to coordinate with your general contractor's schedule.

intro: We take out cabinets, uppers, lowers, vanities and built-ins, and haul them away, without tearing out the rest of the room, anywhere in the St. Louis area. It's for remodels where the walls and floor stay and only the cabinets are being replaced.

sections.h2: Just the cabinets
body: Kitchen uppers and lowers, islands, bathroom vanities, laundry and garage cabinets, pantry units and old built-ins. We unscrew them from the wall and from each other and pull them out, leaving the walls as intact as we can. Countertops come off first and ride on the same truck.
Keeping the cabinets to reuse or sell? Tell us and we'll take them out carefully instead of fast.

sections.h2: How much does cabinet removal cost?
body: Taking them out is labor, quoted per job from photos. Hauling it is priced by the load, from {quarter}. {fit:three-quarter:cabinets} {examplesNote}
Stone countertops are heavy. Old appliances can go on the same truck. {freon}

sections.h2: Before the cabinets come out
body: Empty every cabinet and drawer. Shut off the water to the sink and dishwasher, and have the gas to the range disconnected and capped. Send a photo of each wall of cabinets.

Taking the whole kitchen out? That's [kitchen demolition](/services/demolition/kitchen-demolition/). Just loose cabinets sitting in a garage or basement are a plain [junk removal](/services/junk-removal/) pickup.

name: Fireplace and Chimney Removal
short: Brick and stone fireplaces, hearths, mantels and chimneys removed.
h1: Fireplace and chimney removal in St. Louis, MO
metaTitle: Fireplace & Chimney Removal in St. Louis
metaDescription: Fireplace and chimney removal in St. Louis: brick and stone surrounds, hearths, mantels and chimneys torn out and hauled. Quoted from photos.
intro: We tear out fireplaces and chimneys: brick and stone surrounds, hearths, mantels, inserts and the chimney itself, and haul the masonry away, across St. Louis City, St. Louis County and St. Charles County.

sections.h2: Surround, hearth, mantel or the whole chimney
body: Some jobs are cosmetic: the brick or stone face, the raised hearth and the mantel come off so a new surround can go on. Others take the whole fireplace and the chimney above it. Tell us which you want, and whether the chimney is inside a wall, on an outside wall or through the roof.
A chimney can tie into the framing of the house, so have a contractor look at what happens once it's gone, and who closes up the roof, the wall and the floor afterward.

sections.h2: How much does fireplace removal cost?
body: The tear-out itself is quoted per job. {heavy} The haul starts at {quarter} for a quarter of the truck.

sections.h2: Before the masonry comes down
body: Gas fireplaces and inserts need the gas line shut off and capped by a plumber first. Have the flue cleaned if it's been used recently. Ask your city whether the job needs a permit, and we'll help you sort out what it takes. We don't pull City of St. Louis demolition permits.

Older fireplaces and chimneys can have materials that contain asbestos, like old flue pipe, insulation or the panels around an insert. An inspector should test it before we start. We can't test for, remove or haul asbestos. A painted mantel or brick in a pre-1978 house should be tested for lead as well.

name: Staircase Removal
short: Interior and exterior stairs taken out for the replacement.
h1: Staircase removal in St. Louis, MO
metaTitle: Staircase Removal in St. Louis, MO
metaDescription: Staircase removal in St. Louis: interior and basement stairs, railings and exterior wood steps torn out and hauled, ready for the new staircase.
intro: We take out old staircases, interior stairs, basement stairs, railings and balusters, and wooden exterior steps, and haul the debris away, anywhere in the St. Louis area. It clears the way for your carpenter to build the new set.

sections.h2: Treads, stringers and railings
body: Treads, risers, stringers, the handrail, balusters and the newel post. Keeping the original railing or newel? Tell us and we'll take those off first and set them aside.
Concrete steps outside are a different job: [concrete removal](/services/demolition/concrete-removal/). Steps attached to a deck are part of [deck demolition](/services/demolition/deck-demolition/).

sections.h2: Plan the new stairs first
body: Once the stairs are out, the floor above can't be reached, so have the replacement planned before we start, along with temporary access if you need it. A staircase opening is part of the house's framing; your carpenter or contractor should confirm what stays.
Old stairs are usually painted many times over. Lead paint was sold for homes until 1978, so test old painted surfaces before they're torn out.

sections.h2: Basement, attic and back-porch stairs
body: Basement stairs are a common one: open wooden treads that have worn, cracked or gotten too steep for comfort. Attic pull-down ladders and narrow back stairways come out the same way. Wooden steps off a back door or a side porch are outside work, but the tear-out is the same idea.
Tell us the floor-to-floor height and how wide the opening is, and send a photo from the top and the bottom. That's enough to quote it.

sections.h2: How much does staircase removal cost?
body: The removal is labor, quoted per job from photos. What we haul is priced by the load.
Doing more of the house? See [interior demolition](/services/demolition/interior-demolition/).

metaTitle: Porch Demolition & Removal in St. Louis
metaDescription: Porch demolition in St. Louis: wood porches, porch roofs, railings, screens and steps torn down and hauled away. Labor is quoted from your photos.
intro: We tear down old porches: the floor, framing, railings, screens, steps and the porch roof, and haul the debris away, across St. Louis City, St. Louis County and St. Charles County.

body: Rotted wood porches, enclosed and screened porches, porch roofs and their posts, railings and steps. Tell us what the porch is attached to, and what's staying: the house wall, the roof line above, the foundation piers or the concrete pad.
A concrete stoop or slab porch is [concrete removal](/services/demolition/concrete-removal/). A freestanding deck is [deck demolition](/services/demolition/deck-demolition/).

sections.h2: How much does porch demolition cost?
body: We quote the demolition from your photos. Hauling is priced by the load, starting at {quarter} for a quarter of the truck. {heavy}

body: Porch lights and outlets need the power shut off at the breaker. Plan how you'll get in and out of that door once the porch is gone. Permit rules depend on your city and the job, and we'll walk you through what yours needs. We don't pull City of St. Louis demolition permits.
Porches on older homes are often covered in old paint. Homes built before 1978 can have lead paint, so have painted surfaces tested before demo day and tell us what the results say.

name: Fence Removal

intro: We tear out old fences: wood privacy fences, chain-link and vinyl, with the posts and their concrete footings, and haul it all away, anywhere in the St. Louis area.

sections.h2: Panels, posts and footings
body: Wood pickets and panels, chain-link fabric, rails and posts, vinyl panels, gates and the hardware. Posts set in concrete come out with the footing still on them unless you want them cut at grade. Tell us which you prefer.
Already torn down and stacked? Then it's a haul only: [yard waste and brush removal](/services/junk-removal/yard-waste-removal/) covers old fence boards in the pile.

sections.h2: How much does fence removal cost?

sections.h2: Before the fence comes out

Clearing the yard too? See [shed demolition](/services/demolition/shed-demolition/) and [swing set and playset removal](/services/junk-removal/playset-removal/).

Ask us what happens to the hole afterward, and plan with your landscaper or contractor for fill dirt and grading.

sections.h2: How much does pool removal cost?
body: The demo work is quoted per job from photos. {heavy} The haul is by the load, at {full} for a full {maxYards}-yard truck, and a pool is usually more than one load.
Deck or hot tub next to it? See [deck demolition](/services/demolition/deck-demolition/) and [hot tub removal](/services/demolition/hot-tub-removal/).
